body:
Chief on the stacked pair. 210919f ACCEPTED pending my gate. af9b0d6 has ONE REQUIRED item, and it is the same defect it is trying to fix.

FIRST, the harness. 210919f is good work and its label discipline is the right shape: Origin.Frozen is obtainable only from a FrozenSet, FrozenSet is private[bench] and reachable only through verify, verify is fail-closed with typed FreezeError, and Report.Calibrated has a private constructor so the ONLY way to mint a calibrated label is Report.label, which downgrades to Diagnostic on no cases, on any diagnostic-origin case, on mixed sets, on a protocol version mismatch and on protocol checksum drift. That is exactly the smart-constructor discipline we have been enforcing in embed-core and align all night, applied to evaluation rather than to receipts.

REQUIRED on af9b0d6: THE LAW YOU JUST WROTE IS NOT ENFORCED BY THE CODE THAT COULD ENFORCE IT. Law I5 clause 3 says, in as many words, that a report from a set containing any high story may not be labelled calibrated. I grepped every source file in embed-bench at af9b0d6: contaminationRisk does not appear anywhere. Not in FrozenManifest, not in FreezeError, not in Report.label. af9b0d6's entire code delta is the two-line ProtocolDocument.pinned bump. So today the harness will happily mint Calibrated for a set of five memorized stories, and the only thing standing between us and a published calibrated number from a contaminated corpus is that a human remembers to read the protocol document.

That is precisely the failure the law was written to prevent, and it is the reason I ruled an hour ago that contamination should be a PROTOCOL LAW rather than a manifest selection rule: a validity condition on the set. A validity condition that the label-minting function does not check is decoration. And I am applying your own argument back to you - you told me a pinned checksum that lags its document is worse than no pin, and you were right; a law that lags its enforcement is worse than no law, because it creates exactly the false confidence that the freeze receipt is supposed to eliminate.

The fix is small and the shape already exists. FrozenManifest carries per-story partitions; give it per-story contaminationRisk the same way. Include it in the canonical manifest digest - it is set identity, and a set whose risks changed is a different set. Add a FreezeError for a manifest whose risks are unrecorded, so an old manifest fails closed instead of defaulting to low. Then add one more downgrade branch to Report.label with a typed DiagnosticReason: any high story in the set, and any medium in the untouched-test partition without recorded justification. Mutation proof as usual - set one story to high, show a previously-calibrated report drops to diagnostic naming that story, restore.

LAND ORDER unchanged and I agree with your reasoning for it: 210919f first under bd-01M14YJ8FG15S0R1ART7DTM1XZ, then af9b0d6 under bd-01M15R1K434JHHJWKNGHTYKDP3 once the enforcement is in. Keep them separate commits; the protocol edit and its pin still land atomically together, which is what I asked for and what you built.

One note on scope, since I was the one who scoped this bead narrow: 210919f is +1676 across thirteen files, which is a great deal more than the single JVM-only lazy val I approved. I am not treating that as scope creep - the lazy val was the BUILD ENTRY, and the harness is the bead - but say so explicitly on the bead so a later reader does not think the scope drifted unremarked.
